reviewed_contracts: Scalar cardinality checks count rows, including equal rows and rows split across batches; retained state rejects a second row before storage.
The bound one-column schema widens only root nullability, with static admission also applied to unused branches and empty outer input.
Uncorrelated initialization occurs at first selected demand once per execution; correlated state is fresh per selected outer row.
CASE/COALESCE demand guards preserve selected evaluation and lexical outer scope without promising general Boolean short circuiting.
Native selection and retained-column owners preserve exact typed/nested values and credits; inner operators retain their own admission policies.
Late cardinality errors leave prior batches provisional and writer staging uncommitted; consumer failures, cancellation and resource denials release state.
Python scalar declarations carry declared sources through column, predicate, aggregate and window builders; native SQL remains the executing boundary.
Documentation examples have complete literal row comparisons; current-source support is distinguished from immutable v0.4.0 package contents.
The unchanged acceptance packet retains failed attempts; the independent checker correction is isolated and its other counters remain identical.
limitations: Hosted automated review reports the account review limit; this is not an approval.
Full43 compares retained native results; independent small fixtures establish new scalar semantics.
No performance, complete reader/codec accounting, process-RSS, production or new-release claim.
